source: Marcura Maritime Scope 3 Strategy Report, Section 10 (Implementation Priorities)
report_text: Initial release: License a general-purpose calculation engine and factor database; partner with an AIS-based vessel calculation provider for sea-freight legs; build a maritime procurement taxonomy for the highest-volume Scope 3 category (vessel spares and consumables); ship a single audit-ready report type. Phase two: Extend the taxonomy to additional procurement categories; launch supplier engagement workflows with a pilot group of maritime suppliers; add IMO-aligned KPI reporting benchmarked against established shipping carbon-intensity methodologies; deepen ERP and procurement-system integrations. Phase three: Explore port-services emissions as a defined data category, in partnership with port authorities or logistics data providers given the near-total absence of existing data; pursue independent methodology certification; evaluate AI-assisted invoice classification tuned specifically to maritime procurement line items. Design constraint: Every release should ship as a feature embedded within existing maritime operational workflows, not as a new standalone platform requiring a separate login — buyers with multiple point systems already in place are unlikely to adopt an additional dashboard.

phases.note: Directly consistent with the report's stated initial release scope (license engine, build maritime taxonomy, ship a single audit-ready report type).

Not explicitly phased in the report as a numbered 'Phase 4'; this phase and its label are an inference consistent with the report's Section 6 conclusion that no competitor combines maritime specialisation across multiple hubs, and with this website's own two-hub (Singapore + Dubai) architecture as a first step toward that scale.
